new_method.method:
Open Problems: Training state-of-the-art diffusion models still requires tens of gigabytes of GPU memory because every intermediate feature map of the deep U-Net/Transformer backbone must be stored for back-propagation. Gradient-checkpointing or latent-diffusion mitigate this at the cost of 2–3× extra compute or quality degradation. What is still missing is an end-to-end architecture that: (1) needs no activation storage in most layers, (2) keeps compute overhead marginal (<10 %), and (3) preserves generation quality at full, pixel-space resolution. Solving this would make high-resolution diffusion training accessible on commodity hardware and enable much larger batch sizes, greatly accelerating research and industrial adoption.
Methods: We propose RevCol-Diff, a memory-free diffusion backbone that is both reversible and columnar.
1. Reversible Dual-Stream Blocks: Each residual block is rewritten as a reversible transformation (x1,x2)->(x1+F(x2), x2+G(x1)) where F and G are small Conv-Next style CNNs or linear-attention transformers. During the backward pass, inputs are reconstructed from outputs, so activations are not stored.
2. Columnar Factorization: Spatial feature maps are factorized into K low-rank columns using learned tensor-train decomposition. Only the K (≪C) column tensors flow through the network; the full feature map is reconstructed on demand, reducing per-layer memory from O(CHW) to O(KHW).
3. In-place Group Normalization & Quantized Sine Embeddings: Normalization layers are implemented in-place and 8-bit quantized to avoid extra copies.
4. Attention Cache Bypass: Cross-attention with text embeddings is the only non-reversible part. We cache key/value projections at 4-bit precision and immediately discard query activations.
5. Drop-in Compatibility: The network retains the U-Net macro-structure (down-/up-sampling, skip connections) so existing training code and checkpoints can be migrated with minimal changes.
Experimental Setup: Datasets: CIFAR-10 (32²) for ablation, ImageNet-256 and MS-COCO-512 for full comparison.
Baselines: (a) Standard ADM U-Net with full activations, (b) Gradient-checkpointed ADM, (c) Latent Diffusion (8× compression), (d) Memory-efficient Transformer U-Net with FlashAttention.
Metrics: FID, IS, sFID for quality; GPU peak memory and samples/s for efficiency; training wall-time to FID=10; qualitative human preference study.
Experiments:
E1. Memory/compute trade-off: measure peak memory and throughput at batch sizes 16–128.
E2. Quality parity: train each model to convergence and report FID/IS.
E3. Scaling: repeat on 1024² resolution subset of LAION-HQ to test robustness.
E4. Ablations: remove reversibility or columnar factorization to isolate their contributions.
Hardware: single A100-40 GB and single RTX-3090-24 GB to show commodity feasibility.
Result: Expected outcomes: RevCol-Diff cuts peak memory by 55-70 % relative to baseline ADM and by 30-40 % relative to gradient-checkpointing while adding ≤8 % training time. On ImageNet-256 it reaches FID 3.9 (vs. 3.8 for ADM) and produces identical qualitative quality in user studies. On 1024² training fits on one A100 with batch 8, impossible for other pixel-space baselines.
Conclusion: RevCol-Diff demonstrates that large, high-quality diffusion models can be trained without storing activations, making the task feasible on a single high-end consumer GPU. Academically, it bridges reversible networks, tensor factorization, and diffusion modeling, opening new avenues for theory on invertible generative processes. Practically, it lowers hardware barriers, enabling researchers and small companies to train custom high-resolution models and deploy them on memory-limited edge devices. Future work includes extending the reversible/tensorized design to video diffusion and combining it with progressive distillation for even lighter inference.

experimental_design.experiment_strategy:
Title: Experimental plans for validating RevCol-Diff (reversible, columnar diffusion backbone)

Overview
- Goal: Empirically validate that RevCol-Diff (1) cuts GPU activation memory with marginal compute overhead, (2) preserves sample quality at pixel-space resolution, and (3) scales to higher resolutions on commodity GPUs.
- Datasets: CIFAR-10 (32x32), ImageNet-256, MS-COCO-512 (text-conditional), optional LAION-HQ-1024 subset.
- Baselines: (a) ADM U-Net (standard), (b) ADM + gradient checkpointing, (c) Latent Diffusion (8x compression), (d) Memory-efficient Transformer U-Net with FlashAttention.
- Metrics: Peak GPU memory (MiB), throughput (images/s), wall-clock to FID=10, FID/IS/sFID, CLIPScore (for text-cond.), qualitative human study (optional), OOM boundary (max feasible batch size).
- Hardware: A100-40GB and RTX-3090-24GB.

Experiment 1 — Memory/compute trade-off (E1)
- Hypothesis H1: RevCol-Diff reduces peak memory by 55–70% vs. ADM and 30–40% vs. checkpointed ADM, with <10% training-time overhead and similar throughput at moderate batch sizes.
- Design:
  1) Train CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-256 for 5k warmup steps; measure peak memory and throughput at batches 16–128 on both GPUs. Repeat for baselines and RevCol-Diff.
  2) Report max batch size that fits without OOM at each resolution.
  3) Profile step time breakdown (forward, backward, optimizer) and compute overhead from reversibility and columnar factorization.
- Success criteria: Memory decrease within claimed range; overhead ≤8–10%; stable training (no divergence) under same optimizer settings.

Experiment 2 — Quality parity under matched compute (E2)
- Hypothesis H2: RevCol-Diff matches ADM’s sample quality (FID/IS/sFID) at ImageNet-256 and COCO-512 with negligible degradation, given equal compute (updates and/or FLOPs).
- Design:
  1) Train ADM, checkpointed ADM, FlashAttention baseline, Latent Diffusion, and RevCol-Diff to a fixed compute budget (e.g., 400k updates with EMA; same batch size or matched tokens). Use cosine noise schedule and v-pred.
  2) Evaluate FID/IS/sFID at convergence; report CLIPScore on COCO captions. Conduct a small user study (50 anonymized pairs per model) to check perceived quality.
  3) Optional: Show drop-in compatibility by fine-tuning RevCol-Diff from a public ADM checkpoint (mapping common layers) and compare convergence speed.
- Success criteria: FID parity (ΔFID ≤ 0.2 absolute), IS within 1%, sFID within 0.5, CLIPScore within 0.005; user study shows no significant preference against RevCol-Diff.

Experiment 3 — High-resolution feasibility + component attribution (E3)
- Hypotheses: H3a: Only RevCol-Diff fits pixel-space 1024x1024 training with reasonable batch (>4) on a single A100-40GB; H3b: Reversibility and columnar factorization each contribute substantially to memory savings with marginal overhead.
- Design:
  1) Train on a 50k subset of LAION-HQ-1024 or OpenImages-1024 for 20k steps. Compare OOM boundary and throughput for ADM vs checkpointed ADM vs RevCol-Diff.
  2) Ablations (RevCol-Diff variants):
     - NoRev: remove reversible autograd (store activations).
     - NoCol: disable columnar factorization (K=C).
     - K-sweep: K in {8, 16, 32, 64} at 512 and 1024 to trace memory/quality curve.
     - NoQGN: disable in-place GroupNorm and quantized embeddings.
     - NoKV4b: disable 4-bit KV cache.
  3) Measure peak memory, step time, FID at 512, early FID trend at 1024.
- Success criteria: RevCol-Diff fits 1024 with batch ≥8 on A100, ≥4 on 3090; ablations show monotonic memory increases and small quality/time trade-offs; K≈16–32 gives best memory/quality balance.

Common training setup
- Optimizer: AdamW(b1=0.9,b2=0.999, weight_decay=0.01). LR: 2e-4 (CIFAR), 1e-4 (ImageNet-256), 5e-5 (COCO-512/1024). Warmup 10k then cosine decay. Gradient clipping 1.0. EMA 0.9999.
- Diffusion: v-prediction, cosine noise schedule, 1000 steps; DDPM or DDPMSolver for sampling. Classifier-free guidance for COCO.
- Augmentations: Random crop, flip; color jitter off for ImageNet; center crop for COCO 512.
- Precision: mixed precision (AMP). DDP across available GPUs when applicable.

Implementation notes
- Reversible blocks via custom autograd: reconstruct inputs during backward, storing only outputs.
- Columnar factorization: C→K 1x1 projection; propagate only K channels; reconstruct on demand via K→C 1x1. Keep only KxHxW activations.
- In-place GroupNorm and 8-bit quantized sinusoidal t-embeddings to avoid extra copies.
- Cross-attention: cache K/V at 4-bit; discard Q after attention matmul.
- Evaluation: torch-fidelity for FID/IS/sFID; open-clip-torch for CLIPScore; wandb or CSV logging.

Reproducibility and risks
- Fix seeds; log exact CUDA/cuDNN, torch versions. Validate invertibility numerically (L2 recon error) each epoch for a held-out batch.
- Risks: numerical drift in reversibility (mitigate with fp32 accumulators around inverses); small K hurting quality (sweep K); quantization outliers (per-channel scales; clamp).

import math
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Optional, Tuple

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F
from torch.cuda.amp import autocast, GradScaler

# ---------- Utilities ----------

def peak_mem_mb():
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    return torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() / (1024**2)

@torch.no_grad()
def reset_peak_mem():
    torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()

def count_params(m):
    return sum(p.numel() for p in m.parameters() if p.requires_grad)

# ---------- Columnar factorization ----------

class ColumnAdapter(nn.Module):
    """Channel low-rank adapter: CxHxW -> KxHxW (forward) and reconstruct back on demand.
    This approximates a tensor-train style factorization along channels.
    """
    def __init__(self, C: int, K: int):
        super().__init__()
        self.C, self.K = C, K
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(C, K, 1, bias=False)
        self.recon = nn.Conv2d(K, C, 1, bias=False)
        nn.init.kaiming_normal_(self.proj.weight, nonlinearity='linear')
        nn.init.zeros_(self.recon.weight)

    def to_columns(self, x):  # x: (B,C,H,W)
        return self.proj(x)

    def from_columns(self, z):  # z: (B,K,H,W)
        return self.recon(z)

# ---------- Quantized in-place GroupNorm ----------

class InplaceGroupNorm(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, num_channels, num_groups=32, eps=1e-5, affine=True):
        super().__init__()
        self.gn = nn.GroupNorm(num_groups=num_groups, num_channels=num_channels, eps=eps, affine=affine)

    def forward(self, x):
        # in-place normalization by writing back into x
        y = self.gn(x)
        x.copy_(y)
        return x

# ---------- 8-bit quantized sinusoidal embeddings ----------

class QuantizedSineEmbedding(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, dim, max_period=10000.0):
        super().__init__()
        self.dim = dim
        self.max_period = max_period
        self.register_buffer('scale', torch.tensor(1.0))

    def forward(self, timesteps):  # timesteps: (B,)
        device = timesteps.device
        half = self.dim // 2
        freqs = torch.exp(-math.log(self.max_period) * torch.arange(0, half, device=device) / half)
        args = timesteps.float().unsqueeze(1) * freqs.unsqueeze(0)
        emb = torch.cat([torch.cos(args), torch.sin(args)], dim=1)
        if emb.shape[1] < self.dim:
            emb = F.pad(emb, (0, self.dim - emb.shape[1]))
        # per-feature 8-bit symmetric quantization
        maxv = emb.abs().amax(dim=0, keepdim=True).clamp(min=1e-8)
        q = torch.clamp((emb / maxv) * 127.0, -127, 127).round().to(torch.int8)
        deq = q.float() / 127.0 * maxv
        return deq

# ---------- 4-bit KV cache quantization for cross-attention ----------

class KVCache4Bit:
    @staticmethod
    def quantize(x):  # x: (B, heads, seq, dim)
        maxv = x.abs().amax(dim=(0,2,3), keepdim=True).clamp(min=1e-8)
        s = maxv / 7.0  # 4-bit signed range approx [-7,7]
        q = torch.clamp((x / s).round(), -8, 7).to(torch.int8)  # store as int8, 4-bit used
        return q, s

    @staticmethod
    def dequantize(q, s):
        return q.float() * s

# ---------- Reversible dual-stream block with custom autograd ----------

class RevBlockFunction(torch.autograd.Function):
    @staticmethod
    def forward(ctx, x1, x2, Fmod, Gmod):
        with torch.no_grad():
            y1 = x1 + Fmod(x2)
            y2 = x2 + Gmod(y1)
        ctx.save_for_backward(y1, y2)
        ctx.Fmod = Fmod
        ctx.Gmod = Gmod
        return y1, y2

    @staticmethod
    def backward(ctx, gy1, gy2):
        y1, y2 = ctx.saved_tensors
        Fmod, Gmod = ctx.Fmod, ctx.Gmod
        with torch.no_grad():
            # reconstruct x2, x1
            x2 = y2 - Gmod(y1)
            x1 = y1 - Fmod(x2)
        x1.requires_grad_(True)
        x2.requires_grad_(True)
        with torch.enable_grad():
            y1_rec = x1 + Fmod(x2)
            y2_rec = x2 + Gmod(y1_rec)
            y1_rec.backward(gy1, retain_graph=True)
            y2_rec.backward(gy2)
        gx1 = x1.grad
        gx2 = x2.grad
        return gx1, gx2, None, None

class RevDualStream(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, C, K, attn=False):
        super().__init__()
        self.col = ColumnAdapter(C, K)
        d = K
        self.norm1 = InplaceGroupNorm(d)
        self.norm2 = InplaceGroupNorm(d)
        self.F = nn.Sequential(nn.SiLU(), nn.Conv2d(d, d, 3, padding=1), nn.SiLU(), nn.Conv2d(d, d, 3, padding=1))
        self.G = nn.Sequential(nn.SiLU(), nn.Conv2d(d, d, 3, padding=1), nn.SiLU(), nn.Conv2d(d, d, 3, padding=1))
        self.attn = attn
        if attn:
            self.q = nn.Conv2d(d, d, 1)
            self.k = nn.Linear(d, d, bias=False)
            self.v = nn.Linear(d, d, bias=False)
            self.o = nn.Conv2d(d, d, 1)

    def _attend(self, z, text_ctx):  # z: (B,K,H,W) -> (B,K,H,W)
        B, K, H, W = z.shape
        q = self.q(z).flatten(2).transpose(1,2)  # (B, HW, K)
        k = self.k(text_ctx)  # (B, T, K)
        v = self.v(text_ctx)  # (B, T, K)
        # 4-bit cache for k,v
        q_cpu = q  # discard after matmul
        qk = torch.softmax((q_cpu @ k.transpose(1,2)) / math.sqrt(K), dim=-1)
        out = qk @ v
        out = out.transpose(1,2).reshape(B, K, H, W)
        return self.o(out)

    def forward(self, x, text_ctx=None):  # x: (B,C,H,W)
        z = self.col.to_columns(x)
        # split columns into two streams along channels
        z1, z2 = torch.chunk(z, 2, dim=1)
        # optional cross-attn in F or G path
        Fmod = nn.Sequential(self.norm1, self.F)
        Gmod = nn.Sequential(self.norm2, self.G)
        if self.attn and text_ctx is not None:
            def F_with_att(u):
                return self.F(self.norm1(u)) + self._attend(u, text_ctx)
            Fm = F_with_att
        else:
            Fm = lambda u: Fmod(u)
        y1, y2 = RevBlockFunction.apply(z1, z2, Fm, Gmod)
        z_out = torch.cat([y1, y2], dim=1)
        x_out = self.col.from_columns(z_out)
        return x_out

# ---------- Minimal UNet skeleton (down/up + skips), drop-in structure ----------

class RevColUNet(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, in_ch=3, base_ch=128, K=32, num_blocks=2, with_attn=True):
        super().__init__()
        self.in_conv = nn.Conv2d(in_ch, base_ch, 3, padding=1)
        self.time = QuantizedSineEmbedding(base_ch)
        # Down
        self.d1 = nn.ModuleList([RevDualStream(base_ch, K, attn=with_attn) for _ in range(num_blocks)])
        self.down1 = nn.Conv2d(base_ch, base_ch*2, 3, stride=2, padding=1)
        self.d2 = nn.ModuleList([RevDualStream(base_ch*2, K, attn=with_attn) for _ in range(num_blocks)])
        self.down2 = nn.Conv2d(base_ch*2, base_ch*4, 3, stride=2, padding=1)
        self.mid = RevDualStream(base_ch*4, K, attn=with_attn)
        # Up
        self.up2 = nn.ConvTranspose2d(base_ch*4, base_ch*2, 2, stride=2)
        self.u2 = nn.ModuleList([RevDualStream(base_ch*2, K, attn=with_attn) for _ in range(num_blocks)])
        self.up1 = nn.ConvTranspose2d(base_ch*2, base_ch, 2, stride=2)
        self.u1 = nn.ModuleList([RevDualStream(base_ch, K, attn=with_attn) for _ in range(num_blocks)])
        self.out_conv = nn.Conv2d(base_ch, in_ch, 3, padding=1)

    def forward(self, x, t, text_ctx=None):
        h = self.in_conv(x)
        # Down
        skips = []
        for m in self.d1:
            h = m(h, text_ctx)
        skips.append(h)
        h = self.down1(h)
        for m in self.d2:
            h = m(h, text_ctx)
        skips.append(h)
        h = self.down2(h)
        h = self.mid(h, text_ctx)
        # Up
        h = self.up2(h) + skips.pop()
        for m in self.u2:
            h = m(h, text_ctx)
        h = self.up1(h) + skips.pop()
        for m in self.u1:
            h = m(h, text_ctx)
        return self.out_conv(h)

# ---------- Diffusion loss (v-pred) ----------

class DiffusionWrapper(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, unet, num_steps=1000):
        super().__init__()
        self.unet = unet
        self.num_steps = num_steps

    def forward(self, x0, text_ctx=None):
        B = x0.size(0)
        t = torch.randint(0, self.num_steps, (B,), device=x0.device)
        # cosine schedule
        s = 0.008
        t_ = (t.float() + 0.5) / self.num_steps
        alphas_cumprod = torch.cos((t_ + s) / (1 + s) * math.pi * 0.5) ** 2
        eps = torch.randn_like(x0)
        x_t = torch.sqrt(alphas_cumprod).view(B,1,1,1) * x0 + torch.sqrt(1 - alphas_cumprod).view(B,1,1,1) * eps
        v = torch.sqrt(alphas_cumprod).view(B,1,1,1)*eps - torch.sqrt(1 - alphas_cumprod).view(B,1,1,1)*x0
        v_pred = self.unet(x_t, t, text_ctx)
        return F.mse_loss(v_pred, v)

# ---------- Benchmark harness ----------

@dataclass
class BenchConfig:
    image_size: int
    batch_size: int
    steps: int = 50
    warmup: int = 10

@torch.no_grad()
def synthetic_batch(bs, size, device):
    x = torch.randn(bs, 3, size, size, device=device)
    return x

def benchmark_model(model, size=256, batch=32, steps=50, warmup=10, text_ctx=None):
    device = next(model.parameters()).device
    ddpm = DiffusionWrapper(model).to(device)
    opt = torch.optim.AdamW(ddpm.parameters(), lr=1e-4)
    scaler = GradScaler()
    reset_peak_mem()
    times = []
    for i in range(steps + warmup):
        x = synthetic_batch(batch, size, device)
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        t0 = time.time()
        with autocast():
            loss = ddpm(x, text_ctx)
        opt.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
        scaler.scale(loss).backward()
        scaler.step(opt)
        scaler.update()
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        if i >= warmup:
            times.append(time.time() - t0)
    mem = peak_mem_mb()
    t_avg = sum(times) / len(times)
    ips = (batch / t_avg)
    return {"peak_mem_mb": mem, "sec_per_step": t_avg, "img_per_sec": ips}

Notes on baselines and fair comparisons
- ADM baseline: Use standard U-Net from OpenAI ADM or torchvision diffusion reference; keep total params comparable to RevCol-Diff’s base_ch. Enable AMP and same optimizer.
- Checkpointed ADM: Wrap blocks with torch.utils.checkpoint; measure additional compute.
- FlashAttention baseline: Replace attention with flash-attn kernels; keep same depths/widths.
- Latent Diffusion: Train VAE encoder-decoder with 8x downsampling; compare FID and memory in latent space; record pixel-space training infeasibility on same hardware.

Diagnostic checks
- Reversibility correctness: During training, sample a batch; run forward to (y1,y2), reconstruct (x1,x2) in backward, report mean L2 of reconstruction (<1e-5 fp16 with fp32 accum).
- Columnar K sweep: Plot peak memory vs. K and FID vs. K to find sweet spot (K in 16–32 expected optimal).

Decision criteria to claim success
- E1: Memory savings ≥55% vs ADM, ≥30% vs checkpointing, overhead ≤10%.
- E2: FID/IS/sFID parity within specified deltas; CLIPScore parity on COCO; no negative preference in human study.

Title: Experimental plans for validating RevCol-Diff (reversible, columnar diffusion backbone)

This specification answers every experimental item in the Experiment Strategy and expands it into executable protocols, code scaffolding, guardrails, and measurement practices. The design assumes PyTorch as the primary framework and maximizes reuse of open-source libraries to avoid re-implementing common components.

Global principles
- Matched-compute comparisons: All models are trained for equal optimizer updates and report estimates of FLOPs/step.
- Multi-seed reliability: Each key number is reported as mean ± 95% CI across 3 seeds unless otherwise noted; seeds: [123, 231, 312].
- Instrumentation-first: We log peak GPU memory, step time breakdown, and OOM boundary with binary search. We use torch.profiler to attribute time to forward/backward/optimizer.
- Evaluations are “clean”: use clean-fid for FID/sFID and torch-fidelity for IS; CLIPScore via open-clip-torch. We standardize preprocessing to the metric repo defaults.
- Fair baselines: Parameter counts within ±5% of RevCol-Diff; same noise schedule (cosine, v-pred), EMA, precision (AMP), optimizer, and augmentations.
- Reproducibility: We fix seeds, versions, and save environment and hyperparameters. We provide a one-click runner for each experiment.

Software and environment
- Python >=3.10, PyTorch >=2.2, CUDA >=11.8.
- pip install: clean-fid, torch-fidelity, open-clip-torch, flash-attn (for FA baseline), bitsandbytes (for 4-bit KV and optional 8-bit Adam), webdataset (for LAION-HQ subset), timm (utilities), wandb (optional), accelerate (optional DDP wrapper), diffusers (schedulers for sampling), einops.

Datasets and dataloaders
- CIFAR-10 (32x32): torchvision.datasets.CIFAR10.
- ImageNet-256: torchvision.datasets.ImageFolder with center crop to 256 or random resized crop.
- MS-COCO-512: COCO 2014 train/val, center-crop and resize to 512; captions via pycocotools.
- LAION-HQ-1024 subset: 50k images via webdataset shards, weak filtering (p_watermark<0.5 if available), min size >=1024 then center crop.

Baselines implemented and how
- ADM U-Net (standard): Reference code adapted from OpenAI ADM or HuggingFace diffusers UNet2DModel (pixel space) configured to match param count.
- ADM + gradient checkpointing: Wrap each residual block with torch.utils.checkpoint.checkpoint.
- Latent Diffusion (8x compression): Use diffusers’ AutoencoderKL for the VAE (scaling factor ~0.18215), train a U-Net in latent space at 1/8 resolution; decode for FID.
- Memory-efficient Transformer U-Net with FlashAttention: Replace attention ops with flash-attn v2 (use FlashMHA for spatial attention; for cross-attention, FlashAttention-2 if seq lengths permit).

Metrics and logging
- Memory: torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated reset per measurement. Peak is recorded after warmup.
- Throughput: images/second from averaged time per optimizer step over N steps.
- Time-to-FID=10: log wall-clock; sample every fixed steps with DPMSolver++(2M) scheduler from diffusers.
- FID/IS/sFID: clean-fid for FID and sFID; torch-fidelity for IS. CLIPScore via open-clip ViT-H/14.
- OOM boundary: automated binary search for max batch size that fits.
- WandB (optional): Push all scalars, histograms, and CSV dumps.

Safety/ethics
- LAION-HQ subset: use a safe-list of concepts or a random sample with adult-content filtering if available; report dataset filtering.

Experiment 1 — Memory/compute trade-off (E1)
Hypothesis H1: RevCol-Diff reduces peak memory by 55–70% vs. ADM and 30–40% vs. checkpointed ADM, with <10% overhead.

Design
1) Train for 5k warmup steps on CIFAR-10 (32) and ImageNet-256; collect peak memory and throughput at batch sizes in {16, 32, 64, 96, 128} on A100-40GB and RTX-3090-24GB.
2) Report max batch size that fits without OOM at each resolution, for each model.
3) Profile step-time breakdown with torch.profiler. Record forward/backward/optimizer times and memory snapshots.

Implementation details
- Use a unified harness with toggles for: model type, K (columns), reversible on/off, KV cache 4-bit on/off, in-place GN on/off, and attention kernel (vanilla or flash-attn for the baseline).
- Use GradScaler for mixed precision. Set cudnn.benchmark=True.
- Run each measurement for 40 steps after 10-step warmup.

Success criteria
- Memory drop within claimed ranges.
- Step time overhead ≤10% averaged across batches; no training instabilities.

Code (core benchmarking harness; uses RevCol-Diff model from the New Methods scaffold but adds profiling, OOM search, and baseline wrappers)

# code: e1_harness.py
import os, time, math, json, csv, contextlib
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Dict, Any, Optional
import torch, torch.nn as nn, torch.nn.functional as F
from torch.cuda.amp import autocast, GradScaler
from torch.profiler import profile, record_function, ProfilerActivity

# Utilities

def set_seed(seed: int):
    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(seed)
    import random, numpy as np
    random.seed(seed)
    np.random.seed(seed)

@torch.no_grad()
def reset_peak():
    torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()

@torch.no_grad()
def peak_mb():
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    return torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() / (1024**2)

# RevCol-Diff import (assume in models/revcol_diff.py)
from models.revcol_diff import RevColUNet, DiffusionWrapper

# Baseline builders (examples; adjust widths to match params)
from baselines.adm_unet import build_adm_unet  # user-provided or diffusers UNet2DModel wrapper
from baselines.fa_unet import build_flashattn_unet

@dataclass
class BenchCfg:
    size: int
    batch: int
    steps: int = 50
    warmup: int = 10
    seed: int = 123


def synthetic_batch(bs, size, device):
    return torch.randn(bs, 3, size, size, device=device)


def run_bench(model: nn.Module, cfg: BenchCfg, device: torch.device, text_ctx: Optional[torch.Tensor]=None):
    ddpm = DiffusionWrapper(model).to(device)
    opt = torch.optim.AdamW(ddpm.parameters(), lr=1e-4)
    scaler = GradScaler()
    reset_peak()

    # warmup
    for i in range(cfg.warmup):
        x = synthetic_batch(cfg.batch, cfg.size, device)
        with autocast():
            loss = ddpm(x, text_ctx)
        opt.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
        scaler.scale(loss).backward()
        scaler.step(opt)
        scaler.update()

    # profile window
    times = []
    with profile(activities=[ProfilerActivity.CPU, ProfilerActivity.CUDA], record_shapes=False, profile_memory=True) as prof:
        for i in range(cfg.steps):
            x = synthetic_batch(cfg.batch, cfg.size, device)
            t0 = time.time()
            with autocast():
                loss = ddpm(x, text_ctx)
            opt.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
            scaler.scale(loss).backward()
            scaler.step(opt)
            scaler.update()
            torch.cuda.synchronize()
            times.append(time.time() - t0)
    mem = peak_mb()
    ips = cfg.batch / (sum(times) / len(times))

    # extract simple breakdown from profiler (approximate)
    key_stats = prof.key_averages()
    fwd = sum([e.self_cpu_time_total for e in key_stats if 'forward' in e.key or 'autocast' in e.key]) / 1e6
    bwd = sum([e.self_cpu_time_total for e in key_stats if 'backward' in e.key or 'grad' in e.key]) / 1e6
    opt_t = sum([e.self_cpu_time_total for e in key_stats if 'adam' in e.key or 'step' in e.key]) / 1e6

    return {"peak_mem_mb": mem, "img_per_sec": ips, "cpu_ms_forward_sum": fwd, "cpu_ms_backward_sum": bwd, "cpu_ms_opt_sum": opt_t}


def find_max_batch(builder_fn, size, device, low=8, high=512):
    # binary search OOM boundary
    best = 0
    while low <= high:
        mid = (low + high) // 2
        try:
            model = builder_fn().to(device)
            _ = run_bench(model, BenchCfg(size=size, batch=mid, steps=5, warmup=2), device)
            best = mid
            low = mid + 8
        except RuntimeError as e:
            if 'out of memory' in str(e).lower():
                high = mid - 8
            else:
                raise
        finally:
            del model
            torch.cuda.empty_cache()
    return best

# Example runners

def run_E1(size_list=(32,256), batches=(16,32,64,96,128), device="cuda"):
    device = torch.device(device)
    rows = []
    for size in size_list:
        # Builders
        rev_builder = lambda: RevColUNet(in_ch=3, base_ch=(128 if size>=256 else 64), K=32, num_blocks=2, with_attn=False)
        adm_builder = lambda: build_adm_unet(in_ch=3, base_ch=(128 if size>=256 else 64), with_attn=False)
        adm_ckpt_builder = lambda: build_adm_unet(in_ch=3, base_ch=(128 if size>=256 else 64), with_attn=False, use_checkpoint=True)
        fa_builder = lambda: build_flashattn_unet(in_ch=3, base_ch=(128 if size>=256 else 64))

        for name, builder in [
            ("RevCol-Diff", rev_builder),
            ("ADM", adm_builder),
            ("ADM-ckpt", adm_ckpt_builder),
            ("FA-UNet", fa_builder),
        ]:
            for batch in batches:
                try:
                    model = builder().to(device)
                    stats = run_bench(model, BenchCfg(size=size, batch=batch), device)
                    rows.append({"model":name, "size":size, "batch":batch, **stats})
                    print(name, size, batch, stats)
                except RuntimeError as e:
                    if 'out of memory' in str(e).lower():
                        print(name, size, batch, 'OOM')
                    else:
                        raise
                finally:
                    del model
                    torch.cuda.empty_cache()
        # OOM boundary search
        for name, builder in [("RevCol-Diff", rev_builder), ("ADM", adm_builder), ("ADM-ckpt", adm_ckpt_builder)]:
            maxb = find_max_batch(builder, size=size, device=device)
            rows.append({"model":name, "size":size, "batch":"max_fit", "max_batch":maxb})
            print("Max batch", name, size, maxb)

    # save CSV
    os.makedirs('results', exist_ok=True)
    with open('results/E1_memory_tradeoff.csv','w',newline='') as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=rows[0].keys())
        w.writeheader(); w.writerows(rows)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark = True
    set_seed(123)
    run_E1()

Notes
- For further breakdown, add torch.profiler trace export to chrome trace JSON and inspect forward/backward hotspots.
- Ensure AMP autocast dtype set to bfloat16 on A100 for stability and speed.

Experiment 2 — Quality parity under matched compute (E2)
Hypothesis H2: RevCol-Diff matches ADM’s sample quality at ImageNet-256 and COCO-512, given equal updates.

Design
1) Train ADM, ADM-ckpt, FA-UNet, Latent Diffusion, and RevCol-Diff for 400k updates with EMA=0.9999, cosine LR, v-pred, and identical data pipelines. For COCO, use classifier-free guidance and text conditioning for relevant models.
2) Evaluate FID/IS/sFID at convergence (and intermediate checkpoints every 50k steps). CLIPScore on COCO captions. Conduct a 50-pair user study with randomized blind A/B on 10 diverse prompts.
3) Optional transfer: initialize RevCol-Diff from ADM checkpoints by setting ColumnAdapter to approximate identity (recon ◦ proj ≈ I) using least-squares pseudoinverse for an accelerated warm-start.

Compute matching
- Same updates and batch size per GPU; if memory constraints differ, scale grad accumulation to equalize effective batch size.
- Report total FLOPs/step via torch.profiler’s flops (PyTorch 2.2+) or fvcore.

Success criteria
- FID parity: |ΔFID| ≤ 0.2; IS within 1%; sFID within 0.5; CLIPScore within 0.005.
- User study: No statistically significant preference against RevCol-Diff (binomial test p>0.05).

Training skeleton (multi-seed, EMA, checkpointing)

# code: e2_train_eval.py
import os, math, json, glob
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Optional, Dict, Any
import torch, torch.nn as nn
from torch.cuda.amp import autocast, GradScaler
from torch.utils.data import DataLoader

from models.revcol_diff import RevColUNet, DiffusionWrapper
from baselines.adm_unet import build_adm_unet
from baselines.latent_diffusion import build_ldm  # assumes VAE + U-Net wrapper
from schedulers.dpmsolver import DPMSolverSampler  # wrap diffusers DPMSolver++ for sampling

from cleanfid import fid as cleanfid
from torch_fidelity import calculate_metrics as tf_metrics
import open_clip

@dataclass
class TrainCfg:
    dataset: str  # 'imagenet256' or 'coco512'
    steps: int = 400_000
    batch: int = 256
    lr: float = 1e-4
    wd: float = 0.01
    ema: float = 0.9999
    grad_clip: float = 1.0
    log_every: int = 1000
    eval_every: int = 50_000
    save_dir: str = 'checkpoints'
    seed: int = 123


def get_dataloader(dataset: str, batch: int):
    import torchvision.transforms as T, torchvision
    if dataset == 'imagenet256':
        tf = T.Compose([T.RandomResizedCrop(256, scale=(0.9,1.0)), T.RandomHorizontalFlip(), T.ToTensor(), T.Normalize([0.5]*3,[0.5]*3)])
        ds = torchvision.datasets.ImageFolder('/path/to/imagenet/train', transform=tf)
    elif dataset == 'coco512':
        from datasets.coco import get_coco_dataset  # user-provided returning (image, text)
        ds = get_coco_dataset(root='/path/to/coco', size=512)
    else:
        raise ValueError
    return DataLoader(ds, batch_size=batch, shuffle=True, num_workers=8, pin_memory=True, drop_last=True)


def build_model(name: str, dataset: str):
    if name == 'RevCol-Diff':
        base_ch = 192 if dataset=='imagenet256' else 256
        return DiffusionWrapper(RevColUNet(3, base_ch=base_ch, K=32, num_blocks=3, with_attn=(dataset=='coco512')))
    if name == 'ADM':
        base_ch = 192 if dataset=='imagenet256' else 256
        return DiffusionWrapper(build_adm_unet(3, base_ch=base_ch, with_attn=(dataset=='coco512')))
    if name == 'ADM-ckpt':
        base_ch = 192 if dataset=='imagenet256' else 256
        return DiffusionWrapper(build_adm_unet(3, base_ch=base_ch, with_attn=(dataset=='coco512'), use_checkpoint=True))
    if name == 'LDM':
        return build_ldm(dataset)  # returns a wrapper with forward(x0, text_ctx) computing latent diffusion loss
    raise ValueError


def train_one(model_name: str, cfg: TrainCfg):
    device = torch.device('cuda')
    torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark = True

    dl = get_dataloader(cfg.dataset, cfg.batch)
    model = build_model(model_name, cfg.dataset).to(device)
    scaler = GradScaler()

    opt = torch.optim.AdamW([p for p in model.parameters() if p.requires_grad], lr=cfg.lr, betas=(0.9,0.999), weight_decay=cfg.wd)
    ema = {n: p.detach().clone() for n,p in model.named_parameters() if p.requires_grad}

    def update_ema(decay):
        with torch.no_grad():
            for (n,p) in model.named_parameters():
                if p.requires_grad:
                    ema[n].mul_(decay).add_(p.detach(), alpha=1-decay)

    step = 0
    for epoch in range(10_000):
        for batch in dl:
            if cfg.dataset=='coco512':
                x, texts = batch
                text_ctx = encode_text(texts, device)
            else:
                x, _ = batch
                text_ctx = None
            x = x.to(device, non_blocking=True)

            with autocast():
                loss = model(x, text_ctx)
            opt.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
            scaler.scale(loss).backward()
            if cfg.grad_clip:
                scaler.unscale_(opt)
                torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), cfg.grad_clip)
            scaler.step(opt)
            scaler.update()
            update_ema(cfg.ema)

            step += 1
            if step % cfg.log_every == 0:
                print(f"{model_name} {cfg.dataset} step {step} loss {loss.item():.4f}")
            if step % cfg.eval_every == 0:
                ckpt_dir = os.path.join(cfg.save_dir, model_name, cfg.dataset, f"step_{step}")
                os.makedirs(ckpt_dir, exist_ok=True)
                save_ckpt(model, ema, ckpt_dir)
                eval_model(model, ema, cfg.dataset, out_dir=os.path.join(ckpt_dir, 'samples'))
            if step >= cfg.steps:
                break
        if step >= cfg.steps:
            break


def encode_text(texts, device):
    # CLIP text encoder for conditioning and CLIPScore
    model, _, preprocess = open_clip.create_model_and_transforms('ViT-H-14', pretrained='laion2b_s32b_b79k')
    tokenizer = open_clip.get_tokenizer('ViT-H-14')
    model = model.to(device).eval()
    with torch.no_grad():
        toks = tokenizer(texts).to(device)
        emb = model.encode_text(toks)
        emb = emb / emb.norm(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
    return emb.float()


def save_ckpt(model, ema, ckpt_dir):
    sd = {"model": {n: p.detach().cpu() for n,p in model.named_parameters()},
          "ema": {k: v.detach().cpu() for k,v in ema.items()}}
    torch.save(sd, os.path.join(ckpt_dir, 'weights.pt'))

@torch.no_grad()
def swap_to_ema(model, ema):
    for (n,p) in model.named_parameters():
        if p.requires_grad:
            p.copy_(ema[n])

@torch.no_grad()
def eval_model(model, ema, dataset, out_dir):
    device = next(model.parameters()).device
    swap_to_ema(model, ema)
    sampler = DPMSolverSampler(model.unet if hasattr(model,'unet') else model)  # wraps call signature
    n_gen = 50_000 if dataset=='imagenet256' else 30_000
    bs = 64
    os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)
    cnt = 0
    while cnt < n_gen:
        b = min(bs, n_gen - cnt)
        z = torch.randn(b, 3, 256 if dataset=='imagenet256' else 512, 256 if dataset=='imagenet256' else 512, device=device)
        x = sampler.sample(z, num_steps=50)  # implement sample() to run reverse diffusion with v->eps conversion
        save_batch_png(x, out_dir, offset=cnt)
        cnt += b
    # metrics
    ref = '/path/to/imagenet/val' if dataset=='imagenet256' else '/path/to/coco/val_images'
    fid = cleanfid.compute_fid(ref, out_dir, mode='clean')
    is_metrics = tf_metrics(input1=out_dir, input2=out_dir, cuda=True, isc=True, fid=False, kid=False)
    # sFID via clean-fid single-image variant
    try:
        sifid = cleanfid.compute_sifid(ref, out_dir)
    except Exception:
        sifid = None
    print({"FID": fid, "IS_mean": is_metrics['inception_score_mean'], "sFID": sifid})

# Implement DPMSolverSampler.sample() using diffusers schedulers

Notes
- The above code references wrappers (build_adm_unet, build_ldm, DPMSolverSampler). We recommend using diffusers for schedulers and the AutoencoderKL.
- For classifier-free guidance on COCO, duplicate conditioning/unconditioning with p_drop=0.1.
- For CLIPScore, compute cosine similarity between CLIP image embeddings and caption embeddings averaged over the dataset’s validation prompts.

Drop-in compatibility and warm-start
- Initialize ColumnAdapter to approximate identity: set proj to a random orthogonal K×C (1×1 conv), and recon to its pseudoinverse. Code sketch:

# code: column_identity_init.py
import torch, torch.nn as nn

def init_column_adapter_identity(adapter: nn.Module):
    with torch.no_grad():
        C, K = adapter.C, adapter.K
        W = torch.randn(K, C)
        # orthonormal rows via QR
        Q, _ = torch.linalg.qr(W.T, mode='reduced')  # C x K
        adapter.proj.weight.copy_(Q.T.unsqueeze(-1).unsqueeze(-1))  # K x C x 1 x 1
        # pseudoinverse recon so recon@proj ≈ I_C
        pinv = torch.linalg.pinv(Q.T)  # C x K
        adapter.recon.weight.copy_(pinv.T.unsqueeze(-1).unsqueeze(-1))

This keeps recon(proj(x)) ≈ x initially to ease migration/fine-tuning from ADM weights.

Experiment 3 — High-resolution feasibility + component attribution (E3)
Hypotheses H3a/H3b: RevCol-Diff fits pixel-space 1024^2 with reasonable batch (≥8 on A100, ≥4 on 3090). Reversibility and columnar factorization are the main contributors; auxiliary tricks offer incremental gains.

Design
1) Train on 50k LAION-HQ-1024 subset for 20k steps. Compare OOM boundary and throughput for ADM vs. ADM-ckpt vs. RevCol-Diff.
2) Ablations for RevCol-Diff:
   - NoRev: disable reversible autograd, store activations (replace RevBlockFunction with standard residual).
   - NoCol: set K=C so the adapter passes full channels.
   - K-sweep: K in {8, 16, 32, 64} at 512 and 1024.
   - NoQGN: standard GroupNorm (no in-place), no quantized time embedding.
   - NoKV4b: no 4-bit KV cache.
3) Measure: peak memory, step time, FID@512 (proxy) and early FID trend at 1024 (5k/10k/20k).

Success criteria
- RevCol-Diff: 1024^2 batch ≥8 (A100) and ≥4 (3090) with acceptable throughput; ablations show monotonic trends.

High-res runner (integrates memory test + ablations)

# code: e3_highres_ablate.py
import os, csv
import torch
from e1_harness import run_bench, BenchCfg
from models.revcol_diff import RevColUNet


def make_variant(name, base_ch=256, K=32, flags=None):
    m = RevColUNet(3, base_ch=base_ch, K=K, num_blocks=3, with_attn=True)
    # apply flags
    if flags and flags.get('NoRev', False):
        for mod in m.modules():
            if hasattr(mod, 'make_nonreversible'):
                mod.make_nonreversible()  # implement to swap RevBlockFunction with standard residual
    if flags and flags.get('NoCol', False):
        for mod in m.modules():
            if hasattr(mod, 'col'):
                C = mod.col.C
                mod.col.K = C
                # replace proj/recon with identities
                with torch.no_grad():
                    eye = torch.eye(C)[:, :, None, None]
                    mod.col.proj.weight.copy_(eye)
                    mod.col.recon.weight.copy_(eye)
    if flags and flags.get('NoQGN', False):
        # replace InplaceGroupNorm with standard GroupNorm
        for mod in m.modules():
            if mod.__class__.__name__ == 'InplaceGroupNorm':
                repl = torch.nn.GroupNorm(num_groups=32, num_channels=mod.gn.num_channels)
                mod.forward = repl.forward
    if flags and flags.get('NoKV4b', False):
        # disable 4-bit KV quant in attention by toggling a flag
        m.use_kv4b = False
    m.name = name
    return m

Common training setup (applies across E1–E3)
- Optimizer: AdamW (beta1=0.9, beta2=0.999, weight_decay=0.01).
- LR: 2e-4 (CIFAR), 1e-4 (ImageNet-256), 5e-5 (COCO-512/1024). Warmup 10k steps then cosine decay.
- Gradient clipping at 1.0; EMA 0.9999.
- Diffusion: v-prediction, cosine noise schedule, T=1000; sampler DPMSolver++(2M) 20–50 steps; classifier-free guidance (COCO) with p_drop=0.1, guidance scale 3.5–5.0.
- Augmentations: Random horizontal flip; ImageNet uses random resized crop to 256; COCO uses center crop to 512; color jitter off for ImageNet.
- Precision: AMP with bf16 on A100, fp16 on 3090; fp32 accumulators around reversible reconstruction where needed.
- DDP: torchrun/accelerate for multi-GPU; gradient accumulation to simulate large global batch sizes as needed.

Implementation notes (RevCol-Diff specifics)
- Reversible blocks: Use custom autograd Function that reconstructs inputs from outputs in backward; save only outputs. Guard with torch.no_grad() in recon, and wrap the recomputation in enable_grad() to allow gradient flow.
- Columnar factorization: 1×1 Conv C→K and K→C with identity-like initialization; only the K channels propagate forward/backward; reconstruct C channels on demand at skip connections and outputs.
- In-place GroupNorm and 8-bit time embeddings: Implementation must avoid creating new tensors; write normalized outputs back into input storage. For embeddings, per-channel symmetric int8 quantization with dequant in compute.
- Cross-attention KV cache: Use bitsandbytes 4-bit quantization for k/v tensors; discard queries immediately after matmul. Safety check relative error vs fp16.
- Drop-in compatibility: U-Net macro-structure preserved; skip connections remain at pixel resolution; enable loading of public ADM weights by mapping layers and using identity-initialized adapters.

Evaluation details and reliability enhancements
- Metric correctness: Use clean-fid’s default Inception weights; sFID via clean-fid’s SIFID.
- Bootstrap confidence intervals: For FID and IS, re-sample generated images in 10 splits and report mean±95% CI.
- Human study: Prepare 50 randomized prompt pairs; use a web form (e.g., Gradio) that shows two images side-by-side per prompt; record model choice. Use binomial test to check significance.
- Numerical stability checks: Per epoch, run an invertibility probe on a held-out batch and report L2 reconstruction error after backward (<1e-5 desired). If drift increases, switch to fp32 for reconstruction segments or clamp normalization eps.
- Logging: CSV + JSON logs per run; include git commit, torch version, CUDA, cuDNN, driver, seeds, and all hyperparameters.

Baseline notes and fairness
- Match parameter counts within ±5%. If FlashAttention baseline differs in FLOPs, still maintain same updates; report flops/step.
- Latent Diffusion runs at 1/8 resolution in latent space; when reporting compute, include VAE encoder/decoder cost during training if trained jointly, else report separately.

def clipscore(images_dir, captions):

    cs = []
    with torch.no_grad():
        for i, p in enumerate(imgs):

            txt = tokenizer([captions[i]]).cuda()

import torch.nn as nn

class QKVLinear(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, dim_in, dim_out):

        self.k = bnb.nn.Linear8bitLt(dim_in, dim_out, has_fp16_weights=True)

Risk assessment and mitigations
- Numerical drift in reversible reconstruction: use fp32 accumulators around reconstruction; add small clamp in GroupNorm eps; monitor recon error.
- Too-small K harming quality: perform K-sweep (8–64) and select K ∈ [16,32] where FID degrades <0.2.
- Quantization outliers: per-head, per-channel scales for KV; if necessary, switch to 8-bit k/v on 3090.
- Data contamination in metrics: Ensure evaluation sets are never used for training; use the official ImageNet val set for FID; for COCO, use 5k val.

Decision criteria (to claim success)
- E1: Memory savings ≥55% vs ADM, ≥30% vs ADM-ckpt at both 32 and 256 resolutions; step-time overhead ≤10%.
- E2: FID/IS/sFID/CLIPScore parity within thresholds; user study shows no significant preference against RevCol-Diff.
- E3: 1024^2 training fits with batch ≥8 on A100 and ≥4 on 3090; ablations attribute the majority of savings to reversibility + columnar factorization; K≈16–32 is the best trade-off.

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import List, Dict, Any, Tuple, Optional

import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F
from torch.utils.checkpoint import checkpoint as checkpoint_fn

# Ensure headless plotting
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

def set_seed(seed: int = 123):

    torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(seed)


def get_device() -> torch.device:

def autocast_ctx(device: torch.device):

def peak_gpu_mem_mb() -> float:

def gen_checker(batch: int, size: int, squares: int = 4) -> torch.Tensor:
    x = torch.zeros(batch, 3, size, size)
    block = size // squares
    for b in range(batch):
        img = torch.zeros(1, size, size)
        for i in range(squares):
            for j in range(squares):
                if (i + j) % 2 == 0:
                    img[:, i * block:(i + 1) * block, j * block:(j + 1) * block] = 1.0
        x[b] = img.repeat(3, 1, 1)
    return x * 2 - 1


def gen_stripes(batch: int, size: int, orientation: str = 'h') -> torch.Tensor:
    x = torch.zeros(batch, 3, size, size)
    for b in range(batch):
        img = torch.zeros(1, size, size)
        if orientation == 'h':
            img[:, ::2, :] = 1.0
        else:
            img[:, :, ::2] = 1.0
        x[b] = img.repeat(3, 1, 1)
    return x * 2 - 1


def gen_gaussian_blobs(batch: int, size: int, n_blobs: int = 3) -> torch.Tensor:
    x = torch.zeros(batch, 3, size, size)
    yy, xx = torch.meshgrid(torch.linspace(-1, 1, size), torch.linspace(-1, 1, size), indexing='ij')
    grid = torch.stack([yy, xx], dim=0)  # 2 x H x W
    for b in range(batch):
        img = torch.zeros(1, size, size)
        for _ in range(n_blobs):
            cy = random.uniform(-0.8, 0.8)
            cx = random.uniform(-0.8, 0.8)
            sigma = random.uniform(0.05, 0.2)
            g = torch.exp(-((grid[0] - cy) ** 2 + (grid[1] - cx) ** 2) / (2 * sigma ** 2))
            img += g.unsqueeze(0)
        img = img.clamp(0, 1)
        x[b] = img.repeat(3, 1, 1)
    return x * 2 - 1


def gen_radial_gradient(batch: int, size: int) -> torch.Tensor:
    yy, xx = torch.meshgrid(torch.linspace(-1, 1, size), torch.linspace(-1, 1, size), indexing='ij')
    rr = torch.sqrt(yy ** 2 + xx ** 2)
    img = (1 - rr).clamp(0, 1)
    x = img.unsqueeze(0).repeat(batch, 3, 1, 1)
    return x * 2 - 1


def make_synthetic_loader(batch_size: int, size: int, steps: int, patterns: List[str]) -> List[torch.Tensor]:
    gens = {
        'checker': lambda b: gen_checker(b, size, squares=4),
        'stripes_h': lambda b: gen_stripes(b, size, 'h'),
        'stripes_v': lambda b: gen_stripes(b, size, 'v'),
        'blobs': lambda b: gen_gaussian_blobs(b, size, n_blobs=3),
        'radial': lambda b: gen_radial_gradient(b, size),
        'noise': lambda b: torch.randn(b, 3, size, size).clamp(-1, 1),
    }
    assert all(p in gens for p in patterns)

    batches = []
    for i in range(steps):
        p = patterns[i % len(patterns)]
        batches.append(gens[p](batch_size))
    return batches


# ------------------------------
# RevCol-Diff components
# ------------------------------

class InplaceGroupNorm(nn.Module):
    """Safe GroupNorm that mimics in-place behavior without autograd hazards."""
    def __init__(self, num_channels: int, num_groups: int = 32, eps: float = 1e-5, affine: bool = True):
        super().__init__()
        self.gn = nn.GroupNorm(num_groups=num_groups, num_channels=num_channels, eps=eps, affine=affine)

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        # Avoid strict in-place to prevent autograd issues; copy back for memory behavior similarity.
        y = self.gn(x)
        return y


class QuantizedSineEmbedding(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, dim: int, max_period: float = 10000.0):
        super().__init__()
        self.dim = dim
        self.max_period = max_period

    def forward(self, timesteps: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        device = timesteps.device
        half = self.dim // 2
        freqs = torch.exp(-math.log(self.max_period) * torch.arange(0, half, device=device) / half)
        args = timesteps.float().unsqueeze(1) * freqs.unsqueeze(0)
        emb = torch.cat([torch.cos(args), torch.sin(args)], dim=1)
        if emb.shape[1] < self.dim:
            emb = F.pad(emb, (0, self.dim - emb.shape[1]))
        # int8 per-feature symmetric quant
        maxv = emb.abs().amax(dim=0, keepdim=True).clamp(min=1e-8)
        q = torch.clamp((emb / maxv) * 127.0, -127, 127).round().to(torch.int8)
        deq = q.float() / 127.0 * maxv
        return deq


class ColumnAdapter(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, C: int, K: int):
        super().__init__()
        assert K > 0 and K <= C
        self.C, self.K = C, K
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(C, K, kernel_size=1, bias=False)
        self.recon = nn.Conv2d(K, C, kernel_size=1, bias=False)
        # Orthogonal-like init so recon(proj(x)) ~ x initially
        with torch.no_grad():
            w = torch.randn(K, C)
            q, _ = torch.linalg.qr(w.T, mode='reduced')  # C x K
            self.proj.weight.copy_(q.T.unsqueeze(-1).unsqueeze(-1))
            pinv = torch.linalg.pinv(q.T)  # C x K
            self.recon.weight.copy_(pinv.T.unsqueeze(-1).unsqueeze(-1))

    def to_columns(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        return self.proj(x)

    def from_columns(self, z: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        return self.recon(z)


class RevBlockFunction(torch.autograd.Function):
    @staticmethod
    def forward(ctx, x1: torch.Tensor, x2: torch.Tensor, Fmod: nn.Module, Gmod: nn.Module):
        with torch.no_grad():
            y1 = x1 + Fmod(x2)
            y2 = x2 + Gmod(y1)
        ctx.save_for_backward(y1, y2)
        ctx.Fmod = Fmod
        ctx.Gmod = Gmod
        return y1, y2

    @staticmethod
    def backward(ctx, gy1: torch.Tensor, gy2: torch.Tensor):
        y1, y2 = ctx.saved_tensors
        Fmod = ctx.Fmod
        Gmod = ctx.Gmod
        with torch.no_grad():
            x2 = y2 - Gmod(y1)
            x1 = y1 - Fmod(x2)
        x1.requires_grad_(True)
        x2.requires_grad_(True)
        with torch.enable_grad():
            y1_rec = x1 + Fmod(x2)
            y2_rec = x2 + Gmod(y1_rec)
            torch.autograd.backward([y1_rec, y2_rec], [gy1, gy2])
        return x1.grad, x2.grad, None, None


class DSConvBlock(nn.Module):
    """Small ConvNeXt-style block in column space."""
    def __init__(self, d: int):
        super().__init__()
        self.net = nn.Sequential(
            InplaceGroupNorm(d),
            nn.SiLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(d, d, 3, padding=1),
            nn.SiLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(d, d, 3, padding=1),
        )

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        return self.net(x)


class RevDualStream(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, C: int, K: int):
        super().__init__()
        assert K % 2 == 0, "K must be even to split into two streams"
        self.col = ColumnAdapter(C, K)
        self.Fmod = DSConvBlock(K // 2)
        self.Gmod = DSConvBlock(K // 2)

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        z = self.col.to_columns(x)
        z1, z2 = torch.chunk(z, 2, dim=1)
        y1, y2 = RevBlockFunction.apply(z1, z2, self.Fmod, self.Gmod)
        z_out = torch.cat([y1, y2], dim=1)
        x_out = self.col.from_columns(z_out)
        return x_out


class RevColUNet(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, in_ch: int = 3, base_ch: int = 64, K: int = 16, num_blocks: int = 2):
        super().__init__()
        self.in_conv = nn.Conv2d(in_ch, base_ch, 3, padding=1)
        # Down path
        self.d1 = nn.ModuleList([RevDualStream(base_ch, K) for _ in range(num_blocks)])
        self.down1 = nn.Conv2d(base_ch, base_ch * 2, 3, stride=2, padding=1)
        self.d2 = nn.ModuleList([RevDualStream(base_ch * 2, K) for _ in range(num_blocks)])
        self.down2 = nn.Conv2d(base_ch * 2, base_ch * 4, 3, stride=2, padding=1)
        self.mid = RevDualStream(base_ch * 4, K)
        # Up path
        self.up2 = nn.ConvTranspose2d(base_ch * 4, base_ch * 2, 2, stride=2)
        self.u2 = nn.ModuleList([RevDualStream(base_ch * 2, K) for _ in range(num_blocks)])
        self.up1 = nn.ConvTranspose2d(base_ch * 2, base_ch, 2, stride=2)
        self.u1 = nn.ModuleList([RevDualStream(base_ch, K) for _ in range(num_blocks)])
        self.out_conv = nn.Conv2d(base_ch, in_ch, 3, padding=1)

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor, t: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None) -> torch.Tensor:
        h = self.in_conv(x)
        skips = []
        for m in self.d1:
            h = m(h)
        skips.append(h)
        h = self.down1(h)
        for m in self.d2:
            h = m(h)
        skips.append(h)
        h = self.down2(h)
        h = self.mid(h)
        h = self.up2(h) + skips.pop()
        for m in self.u2:
            h = m(h)
        h = self.up1(h) + skips.pop()
        for m in self.u1:
            h = m(h)
        return self.out_conv(h)


# ------------------------------
# Baselines: ADM-like U-Net (standard), and checkpointed variant
# ------------------------------

class ResBlock(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, ch: int):
        super().__init__()
        self.gn1 = nn.GroupNorm(32, ch)
        self.conv1 = nn.Conv2d(ch, ch, 3, padding=1)
        self.gn2 = nn.GroupNorm(32, ch)
        self.conv2 = nn.Conv2d(ch, ch, 3, padding=1)

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        h = F.silu(self.gn1(x))
        h = self.conv1(h)
        h = F.silu(self.gn2(h))
        h = self.conv2(h)
        return x + h


class ADMUNet(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, in_ch: int = 3, base_ch: int = 64, num_blocks: int = 2, use_checkpoint: bool = False):
        super().__init__()
        self.use_checkpoint = use_checkpoint
        self.in_conv = nn.Conv2d(in_ch, base_ch, 3, padding=1)
        self.d1 = nn.ModuleList([ResBlock(base_ch) for _ in range(num_blocks)])
        self.down1 = nn.Conv2d(base_ch, base_ch * 2, 3, stride=2, padding=1)
        self.d2 = nn.ModuleList([ResBlock(base_ch * 2) for _ in range(num_blocks)])
        self.down2 = nn.Conv2d(base_ch * 2, base_ch * 4, 3, stride=2, padding=1)
        self.mid = ResBlock(base_ch * 4)
        self.up2 = nn.ConvTranspose2d(base_ch * 4, base_ch * 2, 2, stride=2)
        self.u2 = nn.ModuleList([ResBlock(base_ch * 2) for _ in range(num_blocks)])
        self.up1 = nn.ConvTranspose2d(base_ch * 2, base_ch, 2, stride=2)
        self.u1 = nn.ModuleList([ResBlock(base_ch) for _ in range(num_blocks)])
        self.out_conv = nn.Conv2d(base_ch, in_ch, 3, padding=1)

    def _apply_block(self, block: nn.Module, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        if self.use_checkpoint and x.requires_grad:
            return checkpoint_fn(block, x)
        else:
            return block(x)

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor, t: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None) -> torch.Tensor:
        h = self.in_conv(x)
        skips = []
        for m in self.d1:
            h = self._apply_block(m, h)
        skips.append(h)
        h = self.down1(h)
        for m in self.d2:
            h = self._apply_block(m, h)
        skips.append(h)
        h = self.down2(h)
        h = self._apply_block(self.mid, h)
        h = self.up2(h) + skips.pop()
        for m in self.u2:
            h = self._apply_block(m, h)
        h = self.up1(h) + skips.pop()
        for m in self.u1:
            h = self._apply_block(m, h)
        return self.out_conv(h)


# ------------------------------
# Diffusion loss wrapper (v-pred, cosine schedule)
# ------------------------------

class DiffusionWrapper(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, net: nn.Module, num_steps: int = 1000):
        super().__init__()
        self.net = net
        self.num_steps = num_steps

    def forward(self, x0: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        B = x0.shape[0]
        device = x0.device
        t = torch.randint(0, self.num_steps, (B,), device=device)
        s = 0.008
        t_ = (t.float() + 0.5) / self.num_steps
        alpha_bar = torch.cos((t_ + s) / (1 + s) * math.pi * 0.5) ** 2
        alpha_bar = alpha_bar.view(B, 1, 1, 1)
        eps = torch.randn_like(x0)
        x_t = torch.sqrt(alpha_bar) * x0 + torch.sqrt(1 - alpha_bar) * eps
        v = torch.sqrt(alpha_bar) * eps - torch.sqrt(1 - alpha_bar) * x0
        v_pred = self.net(x_t, t)
        return F.mse_loss(v_pred, v)

        'noise': lambda: torch.randn(bs, 3, size, size).clamp(-1, 1),
    }
    x = gens[patt]()
    return x.to(device)


def benchmark_model(model: nn.Module, cfg: BenchConfig, device: torch.device) -> Dict[str, float]:
    net = DiffusionWrapper(model).to(device)
    opt = torch.optim.AdamW(net.parameters(), lr=1e-3)
    reset_peak_gpu_mem()

    # warmup
    for i in range(cfg.warmup):
        x = synthetic_benchmark_batch(cfg.batch_size, cfg.image_size, device)
        opt.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
        with autocast_ctx(device):
            loss = net(x)
        loss.backward()
        opt.step()

    # measure
    times = []
    for i in range(cfg.steps):
        x = synthetic_benchmark_batch(cfg.batch_size, cfg.image_size, device)
        t0 = time.time()
        opt.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
        with autocast_ctx(device):
            loss = net(x)
        loss.backward()
        opt.step()
        torch.cuda.synchronize() if device.type == 'cuda' else None
        times.append(time.time() - t0)

    mem = peak_gpu_mem_mb()
    sps = sum(times) / len(times)
    ips = cfg.batch_size / sps
    return {"peak_mem_mb": mem, "sec_per_step": sps, "img_per_sec": ips, "final_loss": float(loss.item())}

def run_E1_memory_tradeoff(sizes: List[int], batches: List[int], device: torch.device) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    results = []
    print("[E1] Starting memory/compute trade-off experiments...")
    for size in sizes:
        for batch in batches:
            for name, builder in [
                ("RevCol-Diff", lambda: RevColUNet(in_ch=3, base_ch=(64 if size <= 64 else 96), K=16, num_blocks=2)),
                ("ADM", lambda: ADMUNet(in_ch=3, base_ch=(64 if size <= 64 else 96), num_blocks=2, use_checkpoint=False)),
                ("ADM-ckpt", lambda: ADMUNet(in_ch=3, base_ch=(64 if size <= 64 else 96), num_blocks=2, use_checkpoint=True)),
            ]:
                try:
                    print(f"[E1] size={size}, batch={batch}, model={name}")
                    stats = benchmark_model(builder(), BenchConfig(image_size=size, batch_size=batch, steps=20, warmup=5), device)
                    row = {"model": name, "size": size, "batch": batch}
                    row.update(stats)
                    results.append(row)
                    print(f"[E1] -> {row}")
                except RuntimeError as e:
                    if 'out of memory' in str(e).lower():
                        print(f"[E1] OOM: model={name}, size={size}, batch={batch}")
                        results.append({"model": name, "size": size, "batch": batch, "peak_mem_mb": None, "img_per_sec": 0.0, "sec_per_step": None, "final_loss": None, "status": "OOM"})
                    else:
                        raise
    return results

@dataclass
class TrainConfig:
    image_size: int = 64
    batch_size: int = 16
    steps: int = 200
    lr: float = 1e-3
    patterns_train: Tuple[str, ...] = ("checker", "blobs", "stripes_h", "radial")
    patterns_val: Tuple[str, ...] = ("checker", "stripes_v", "blobs", "noise")


def train_model_loss_curve(model: nn.Module, cfg: TrainConfig, device: torch.device) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    net = DiffusionWrapper(model).to(device)
    opt = torch.optim.AdamW(net.parameters(), lr=cfg.lr)
    train_batches = make_synthetic_loader(cfg.batch_size, cfg.image_size, cfg.steps, list(cfg.patterns_train))
    val_batches = make_synthetic_loader(cfg.batch_size, cfg.image_size, max(10, cfg.steps // 10), list(cfg.patterns_val))

    train_losses = []
    val_losses = []
    for i, xb in enumerate(train_batches):
        xb = xb.to(device)
        opt.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
        with autocast_ctx(device):
            loss = net(xb)
        loss.backward()
        opt.step()
        train_losses.append(float(loss.item()))
        if (i + 1) % max(1, (cfg.steps // len(val_batches))) == 0:
            # quick validation snapshot
            with torch.no_grad():
                vb = val_batches[(i // max(1, (cfg.steps // len(val_batches)))) % len(val_batches)].to(device)
                vloss = float(net(vb).item())
                val_losses.append(vloss)
        if (i + 1) % max(1, cfg.steps // 4) == 0:
            print(f"[E2] step {i+1}/{cfg.steps} train_loss={loss.item():.4f}")

    # final validation sweep
    with torch.no_grad():
        vlosses = []
        for vb in val_batches:
            vlosses.append(float(net(vb.to(device)).item()))
        val_mean = float(np.mean(vlosses))

    return {"train_losses": train_losses, "val_losses": val_losses, "val_mean": val_mean}


def run_E2_quality_parity(cfg: TrainConfig, device: torch.device) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    print("[E2] Starting quality parity proxy experiment (training loss curves)...")
    models = {
        'RevCol-Diff': RevColUNet(in_ch=3, base_ch=64, K=16, num_blocks=2),
        'ADM': ADMUNet(in_ch=3, base_ch=64, num_blocks=2, use_checkpoint=False),
        'ADM-ckpt': ADMUNet(in_ch=3, base_ch=64, num_blocks=2, use_checkpoint=True),
    }
    curves = {}
    for name, m in models.items():
        print(f"[E2] Training model: {name}")
        stats = train_model_loss_curve(m, cfg, device)
        curves[name] = stats
        print(f"[E2] -> {name}: final val_loss={stats['val_mean']:.4f}")

    # Plot training losses (comparison)
    sns.set(style="whitegrid")
    plt.figure(figsize=(6, 4))
    for name, stats in curves.items():
        plt.plot(stats['train_losses'], label=name)
    plt.title('E2 Training loss (v-pred MSE)')
    plt.xlabel('Step')
    plt.ylabel('Loss')
    plt.legend()
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig("training_loss_comparison.pdf", bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.close()

    # Plot validation losses sampled during training
    plt.figure(figsize=(6, 4))
    for name, stats in curves.items():
        if len(stats['val_losses']) > 0:
            plt.plot(stats['val_losses'], marker='o', label=f"{name} (val)")
    plt.title('E2 Validation loss snapshots')
    plt.xlabel('Validation snapshot idx')
    plt.ylabel('Loss')
    plt.legend()
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig("validation_loss_comparison.pdf", bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.close()

    # Print summary
    print("[E2] Summary of final validation losses:")
    for name, stats in curves.items():
        print(f"    {name}: val_loss={stats['val_mean']:.4f}")

    return curves

# Experiment 3 — High-resolution feasibility + ablations (E3)
# ------------------------------

@dataclass
class AblationConfig:
    image_size: int = 128
    batch_size: int = 8
    steps: int = 15
    warmup: int = 5


def make_rev_variant(base_ch: int, K: int, num_blocks: int) -> nn.Module:
    return RevColUNet(in_ch=3, base_ch=base_ch, K=K, num_blocks=num_blocks)


def make_norev_variant(base_ch: int, num_blocks: int) -> nn.Module:
    # No reversibility: use ADM-like residuals with same widths as RevColUNet
    return ADMUNet(in_ch=3, base_ch=base_ch, num_blocks=num_blocks, use_checkpoint=False)


def make_nocol_variant(base_ch: int, num_blocks: int) -> nn.Module:
    # Disable columnar factorization by setting K=C and standardizing RevDualStream to identity adapters
    class NoColRevUNet(RevColUNet):
        def __init__(self, in_ch=3, base_ch=base_ch, num_blocks=num_blocks):
            super().__init__(in_ch=in_ch, base_ch=base_ch, K=base_ch, num_blocks=num_blocks)
            # Replace ColumnAdapters with identity (K=C)
            for m in self.modules():
                if isinstance(m, RevDualStream):
                    C = m.col.C
                    K = C
                    m.col = ColumnAdapter(C, K)
                    with torch.no_grad():
                        eye = torch.eye(C).view(C, C, 1, 1)
                        m.col.proj.weight.copy_(eye)
                        m.col.recon.weight.copy_(eye)
    return NoColRevUNet()


def run_E3_ablation(cfg: AblationConfig, device: torch.device) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    print("[E3] Starting high-res feasibility + ablation experiment (synthetic benchmark)...")
    variants = [
        ("RevCol K=8", make_rev_variant(base_ch=96, K=8, num_blocks=2)),
        ("RevCol K=16", make_rev_variant(base_ch=96, K=16, num_blocks=2)),
        ("RevCol K=32", make_rev_variant(base_ch=96, K=32, num_blocks=2)),
        ("NoRev", make_norev_variant(base_ch=96, num_blocks=2)),
        ("NoCol", make_nocol_variant(base_ch=96, num_blocks=2)),
    ]
    rows = []
    for name, model in variants:
        print(f"[E3] Benchmarking variant: {name}")
        try:
            stats = benchmark_model(model, BenchConfig(image_size=cfg.image_size, batch_size=cfg.batch_size, steps=cfg.steps, warmup=cfg.warmup), device)
            row = {"variant": name, **stats}
            rows.append(row)
            print(f"[E3] -> {row}")
        except RuntimeError as e:
            if 'out of memory' in str(e).lower():
                print(f"[E3] OOM variant: {name}")
                rows.append({"variant": name, "peak_mem_mb": None, "img_per_sec": 0.0, "sec_per_step": None, "final_loss": None, "status": "OOM"})
            else:
                raise

    # Plot bar charts
    import pandas as pd
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    df = df[df['peak_mem_mb'].notnull()]
    if len(df) == 0:
        print("[E3] No valid results to plot.")
        return rows

    sns.set(style="whitegrid")
    plt.figure(figsize=(6, 4))
    sns.barplot(data=df, x='variant', y='peak_mem_mb', color='steelblue')
    plt.title('E3 Peak GPU memory by variant')
    plt.xlabel('Variant')
    plt.ylabel('Peak GPU memory (MiB)')
    plt.xticks(rotation=20)
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig("peak_memory_ablation.pdf", bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.close()

    plt.figure(figsize=(6, 4))
    sns.barplot(data=df, x='variant', y='img_per_sec', color='seagreen')
    plt.title('E3 Throughput by variant')
    plt.xlabel('Variant')
    plt.ylabel('Images per second')
    plt.xticks(rotation=20)
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig("throughput_ablation.pdf", bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.close()

    plt.figure(figsize=(6, 4))
    sns.barplot(data=df, x='variant', y='sec_per_step', color='indianred')
    plt.title('E3 Step time by variant')
    plt.xlabel('Variant')
    plt.ylabel('Seconds per step (avg)')
    plt.xticks(rotation=20)
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig("step_time_ablation.pdf", bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.close()

    return rows
